key_insight: LLM-guided evolutionary program synthesis can discover interpretable fermion-to-qubit encodings with verified higher distance and better compression than prior Generalized Superfast Encoding constructions.
engineering_relevance: For quantum simulation workflows, the approach suggests a practical way to co-design encoding rules and resource tradeoffs while preserving exact stabilizer-coset correctness.
method: An LLM edits encoding-constructor programs in an evolutionary loop.
An external verifier scores candidates by exact code distance and compression metrics.
High-scoring programs are retained and re-mutated; a second search uses verifier feedback to refine structure.
evidence_signal: The search found molecular-instance GSE encodings with exact distance 5 and one 20-mode case with distance 6, while reducing data-qubit usage by 4.2–5.0× and logical-failure rates by 3.4–8.2× versus the comparison route.
watch_item: The gains are demonstrated on tested instances and resource descriptors only, without claiming circuit-level fault tolerance or Trotter-cost improvement.
paper_title: Evolving Quantum Error-Correcting Encodings for Molecular Simulation
